sections.heading: What makes permanent makeup safer?
paragraphs: Permanent makeup involves the skin, so safety is the whole appointment, not one step of it: a clean studio, fresh disposable barriers, single-use tools, careful pigment handling, gloves, masks, and clear aftercare.
You should know how the space is prepared, what tools are used, and what to do before and after. Ask anything. A question before booking is always welcome.

callout.title: My approach
callout.text: I do not want permanent makeup to feel rushed or unclear. Before we begin, the space is prepared, the service is reviewed, and every tool for your appointment is handled with care.

sections.heading: One client at a time.
sections.lede: Detailed work needs a calm, controlled room. A private appointment keeps the focus on your service, your comfort and your safety.

items.title: Why privacy matters
bullets: No crowded appointment space
No traffic around the work area
Full attention on detailed work
A calmer experience for a personal service

items.title: Why control matters
bullets: Fresh setup for every appointment
Work area cleaned before the service begins

Clear steps during the session

sections.heading: Clean before every client.
sections.lede: Clean surfaces, fresh barriers and a careful setup reduce contact with the treatment area and the tools.

image.shot: Disposable barriers going onto the bed and tray before an appointment

items.label: Surfaces
items.title: Clean surfaces
items.text: Disinfected and prepared between clients, so the appointment starts with a clean work area.

items.label: Barriers
items.title: Fresh barriers
items.text: Disposable barriers protect surfaces and are replaced for each session.

items.label: Protection
items.title: Protective setup
items.text: Gloves, masks and protective coverings are part of every appointment.

callout.title: What this means for you
callout.text: You should never have to wonder whether the room is ready. Clean setup and fresh barriers are part of the service, not a request.

sections.heading: Single-use, then gone.
sections.lede: Single-use tools cut cross-contamination risk because they touch one client and are then safely discarded.

items.title: Needles and cartridges
items.text: New for your appointment, and opened in front of you so you know they have touched no one else.

items.title: Pigment containers
items.text: One cup per client. Pigment is never shared or returned to a bottle.

items.title: Disposable supplies
items.text: Used during the appointment and discarded after it, so the process resets between clients.

items.title: No reuse, ever
items.text: Anything designed for single use is disposed of after the appointment. It is never cleaned and reused.

sections.heading: Your preparation matters too.
sections.lede: A safe appointment is not only the studio. Your skin, your timing, your health history and your aftercare all count.

items.title: Arrive with healthy skin
items.text: Do not book over sunburn, cuts, irritation, breakouts, cold sores or open skin.

items.title: Share health details
items.text: Medications, allergies, healing concerns or medical conditions, before we start.

items.title: Plan your timing
items.text: Not right before a wedding, a vacation, a photo shoot or another big event.

items.title: Follow aftercare
items.text: It protects the treated area and gives the best healed result.

callout.title: Before your appointment
callout.text: Ask first if you recently had filler, Botox, laser, a chemical peel, waxing, brow or lip treatments, an eye procedure, scalp treatments, or other cosmetic work near the area.

sections.heading: Who should ask first.

title: Aftercare.
lede: Permanent makeup can look darker, brighter, sharper, dry, flaky or uneven while it heals. That is normal for many clients, so do not judge the final color too early.
meta: What to expect after brows, eyeliner, lash enhancement, lip tint and scalp micropigmentation.

lead.shot: Aftercare kit on a white towel: sealed cotton swabs, the recommended balm, a printed instruction card

items.title: Do not pick
items.text: Let dryness or flaking release on its own.

items.title: Keep it clean
items.text: Clean hands, clean cotton swabs, the instructions you were given.

items.title: Avoid irritation
items.text: No makeup, heavy sweating, soaking or strong skincare while healing.

items.title: Wait for healing
items.text: Color can change before the final result settles.

sections.heading: What is normal after permanent makeup?
paragraphs: Fresh pigment usually looks darker, sharper or brighter right after the appointment. It has not yet settled into the healed skin.
As the skin heals, the area can look dry, flaky, lighter or patchy. That can read as fading, but much of it is the surface healing stage.
Healed results can take several weeks. The touch-up reviews the healed color, shape and softness, and any area that needs more pigment.

image.shot: Powder brows the morning after the appointment, crisp and dark, before any flaking

callout.title: My advice
callout.text: Do not judge your final result during the first few days. Permanent makeup often looks darker at first, then lighter, then softer as healing continues.

sections.heading: The healing timeline.
sections.lede: Every client heals differently, but this is what many experience.

image.shot: One healing brow in three frames, side by side: day one, day five, week six

items.label: Day 1
items.title: Darker than the finish
items.text: The color looks darker, sharper, brighter or more intense than the healed result.

items.label: Days 2 to 7
items.title: Dry and flaky
items.text: Dryness, tightness, light flaking or temporary patchiness while the skin heals.

items.label: Weeks 2 to 6
items.title: Settled
items.text: The color softens and settles. The touch-up refines the result if needed.

callout.title: Usually a two-step process
callout.text: The first appointment creates the foundation. The touch-up lets me review retention and refine color, shape, softness or density after healing.

sections.heading: What to avoid while it heals.
sections.lede: Follow the instructions for your service. In general, avoid anything that can irritate, soak, contaminate or fade the area.

items.title: Touching and picking
bullets: No fingers on the healing area
No rubbing, scratching, picking or peeling
Let flakes release naturally
A clean cotton swab for any recommended product

items.title: Water, heat and sweat
bullets: No pools, Jacuzzis or open water
No sauna, steam or heavy sweating
No soaking the treated area
Protect the area before bathing if instructed

items.title: Makeup and cosmetic treatments
bullets: No makeup directly on the area
No tinting, lashes, brow or lip products until cleared
No peels, laser, waxing or exfoliation too soon

items.title: Sun and strong skincare
bullets: No sun exposure while healing
Sun protection afterwards helps prevent fading
No AHAs, acids, retinoids or exfoliants nearby
Check labels on active skincare

callout.title: When to contact a physician
callout.text: If you experience excessive redness, swelling, tenderness, elevated temperature, purulent drainage, or signs of infection, contact your physician. If itching, swelling, blistering, or a reaction happens after using an aftercare product, stop using it and ask for guidance.

sections.heading: Brows.
sections.lede: Microblading, powder brows and shading can look dramatic at first: dark, crisp, dry, flaky, light or patchy. At the touch-up I review retention, fill lighter areas, adjust softness and refine the final brow.

sides.title: What is normal
bullets: Darker and sharper right after
Flaking can look like fading
Very light before it settles
Several weeks to the healed result

sides.title: What to avoid

callout.title: Ask before booking eye services
callout.text: Ask before booking if you have active eye irritation, recent eye surgery, certain eye medications, recent cosmetic eye treatments, or sensitivity around the eyes.

sections.heading: Lips.
sections.lede: Lip tint often looks brighter at first. The healed color is usually softer and more natural.

items.title: What is normal

Lighter before it settles

callout.title: Cold sore reminder
callout.text: If you have ever had a cold sore, tell the studio before booking lip tint. Lip tattooing may trigger a cold sore for some clients. For medical guidance, speak with your healthcare provider.

sections.heading: Scalp.
sections.lede: Scalp micropigmentation builds the look of fuller density with tiny pigment impressions. Darker at first, blended as it heals.

items.title: What is normal
bullets: More noticeable right after the session
Pigment softens as the scalp heals
More sessions may be needed for density
Sun exposure fades pigment faster over time

items.title: What to avoid
bullets: Scratching or picking the scalp
Sunburn before and after the appointment
Heavy sweating, soaking, sauna or swimming
Scalp products too soon, without asking

callout.title: About SMP sessions
callout.text: SMP often builds in layers. A consultation decides the treatment area, density goal, hairline plan and how many sessions you may need.

sections.heading: Why touch-ups matter.
sections.lede: Touch-ups complete the process: a review of what your skin kept after healing, then careful refinements.

items.title: Color refresh
items.text: Adds color where the healed result looks too soft or light.

items.title: Shape refinement
items.text: Brows, eyeliner, lips and SMP can be refined once the healed result shows.

items.title: Softness check
items.text: The healed result should look balanced, not too harsh or heavy.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text: Yearly touch-ups refresh pigment after natural fading.

sections.heading: Aftercare questions.
sections.lede: The ones asked most, answered short.

items.q: Why does it look so dark at first?
items.a: Fresh pigment often looks darker, sharper or brighter right after the appointment. It usually softens as the skin heals.
Light flaking or dryness can be normal for some services. Do not pick, peel or scratch; let it release on its own.

items.q: Why does the color look like it disappeared?
items.a: Lighter during healing does not always mean the pigment is gone. It can soften, settle and sometimes return more visibly as healing continues.

items.q: How long does it take to heal?
items.a: Visible healing takes about 1 to 2 weeks, the final color several weeks. Brows may need 4 to 6 weeks before they can be fully evaluated.

items.q: When should I contact the studio?
items.a: When unsure about aftercare, products, healing or touch-up timing. For signs of infection or medical concerns, contact your physician.
Most services are a two-step process. The touch-up reviews retention and refines color, shape, softness or density.

sections.heading: An aftercare question?
sections.text: Call or write if you are unsure about healing, aftercare, touch-up timing, or whether what you are seeing is normal.
